newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: OAU chief urges second term for Africa as U.N. head.
newsitem.headline: OAU chief urges second term for Africa as U.N. head.

text.p: Cameroon's President Paul Biya, chairman of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU), said on Thursday Africa should have a second term as U.N. secretary-general and recommended the candidacy of Boutros Boutros-Ghali, whom the United States has threatened to veto.
In a speech to the General Assembly, Biya reiterated the position taken at a summit meeting of the OAU held in Yaounde, Cameroon, in July.

The African heads of state and government "have requested me to undertake the necessary demarches to the states members of the United Nations to ensure that a second five-year term be given to Africa," he said.
"In this connection, they recommended the candidature of Mr Boutros Boutros-Ghali," he added, referring to the Egyptian incumbent.
"We trust that the members of our organisation will thus enable Africa hold two successive terms at the head of the United Nations, just as in the past Asia, Europe and Latin America did," Biya said.
He was referring to the two terms served by each of Boutros-Ghali's predecessors -- Javier Perez de Cuellar of Peru, Kurt Waldheim of Austria and U Thant of Burma.

The OAU decision was widely interpreted at the time as placing greater emphasis on a second term for Africa than on endorsing the specific candidacy of Boutros-Ghali, whose current term expires at the end of this year.
The United States says a new secretary-general is needed to reform the world body and that it is prepared to use its veto to block Boutros-Ghali's re-election.
A secretary-general is appointed by the 185-nation General Assembly on the recommendation of the 15-nation Security Council, which is expected to begin considering the matter next month.
